text:
Kira: Heads-up — CI started failing on a sampleapp with strict pyright when we pass keywords into autogenerated models during async client setup. Minimal repro below.

Kira: repro:
```py
# runtime (autogen)
class Item(BaseModel):
    id: str
    tags: Optional[list[str]] = None

async def make():
    # pyright error: "Argument 'tags' not found in constructor"
    it = Item(id='i1', tags=None)
    return await AsyncClient.create(item=it)
```

Ben: Interesting. Does the wheel include .pyi files? We used to generate stubs but packaging recently changed and I think pyi are not bundled for some nested modules. If the published stub has a positional-only __init__ or different signature, type checkers will reject kw args.

Oscar: I pulled the installed package and the generated pyi for Item shows `def __init__(self, id: str) -> None: ...` (no tags kw). Runtime has default for tags. So mismatch. pyright treats that as missing kw param.

Marlene: Short-term workaround: sampleapps can use positional args or `# type: ignore` on the line. But we should avoid recommending that to customers.

Kira: Created issue https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/5611 with the sampleapp and CI config that reproduces it. Marked label dx:typing.

Ben: Long-term fix options: 1) include accurate .pyi stubs that mirror runtime defaults and Optional types; 2) change codegen to emit __init__ signatures that accept keywords (e.g., keyword-only or accept **kwargs and cast); 3) add an integration mypy/pyright job that runs against sampleapps in CI to catch regressions.

Oscar: I'll open a packaging PR to ensure .pyi files are included and add a smoke mypy check for the sampleapp. If tests pass we can backport to 0.13.x.

CI Bot: CI: sampleapps/strict-typing failed on pyright step. Linked issue #5611.

Marlene: Triage notes: severity=medium, owner=@Oscar, workaround=positional args or type ignore, docs: add a note in SDK upgrade guide.

Kira: Thanks — will update the issue with a tiny patch demonstrating the stubs fix and ping when PR is ready. :thumbsup:
